summary: Determine precisely what quorum=all enforces in DRBD-9: does a 2-of-4 minority actually keep writing / mint UUIDs, or only the metadata bump slips past suspend-io?

final.what_it_enforces: quorum=all + on-no-quorum=suspend-io freezes the entire APPLICATION/DATA path on a minority partition: no user/application byte can reach the local backing disk or any peer, so a 2-of-4 minority cannot build a divergent committed data set. That is the whole point and it holds. Two independent gates enforce it, both keyed on drbd_suspended() (which ORs in susp_quorum, set true exactly when on_no_quorum==suspend-io AND the partition lacks quorum — drbd_state.c:2473-2474): (1) ENTRY gate — a new app bio entering __drbd_make_request blocks in inc_ap_bio's wait_event because may_inc_ap_bio() returns false while suspended (drbd_int.h:2901-2906), so no request/bio is even built; (2) SUBMIT gate — any already-built request hitting drbd_send_and_submit is marked RQ_POSTPONED, has its private_bio bio_put/NULLed, and `goto out` BEFORE drbd_submit_req_private_bio() (the only thing that submits to ldev->backing_bdev) is ever reached — VERIFIED verbatim at /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd/drbd_req.c:2057-2066. Postponed writes are re-queued and loop until quorum returns: never errored-to-disk, never silently dropped. The QOU_ALL threshold itself is VERIFIED at drbd_state.c:1369-1370 (`case QOU_ALL: quorum_at = voters;`), so 2-of-4 is correctly quorum-less. Guarantee source is both the code AND LINBIT's contract, which is scoped to the replicated data set ('a node that does not have quorum needs to guarantee that the replicated data set is not touched, so that the node does not create a diverging data set'; suspend-io 'suspends all queued and future I/O operations to the backing DRBD device').
final.what_it_does_not_enforce: It does NOT freeze the internal current-UUID rotation, because that is a METADATA write on a completely different code path. On quorum/peer-data loss the state machine arms NEW_CUR_UUID: create_new_uuid is set when a Primary loses contact with a peer's data while its OWN disk is still UpToDate — gated on role==R_PRIMARY && drbd_data_accessible() (local disk UpToDate), NOT on have_quorum (VERIFIED drbd_state.c:3096-3136). The bump is then executed from the after-state-change / worker path by calling drbd_uuid_new_current(device,false) at drbd_state.c:3807 and :4471 (VERIFIED) — and these two call sites carry NO drbd_suspended()/have_quorum guard, unlike the worker dispatch at drbd_sender.c:3443 which IS gated `if (device->have_quorum[NOW] && drbd_data_accessible(device, NOW))`. The leaf __new_current_uuid_prepare (VERIFIED /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd/drbd_main.c:4947-4977) does get_random_u64() + __drbd_uuid_set_current() + drbd_md_sync(), persisting a fresh metadata superblock to the SEPARATE metadata device (ldev->md_bdev) via its own directly-submitted bio (drbd_actlog.c _drbd_md_sync_page_io, REQ_OP_WRITE) that never goes through __drbd_make_request / inc_ap_bio / drbd_suspended. Direct inspection confirms the leaf body has no suspend/quorum/may_inc_ap_bio check. The 'new current UUID: %016llX weak: %016llX' kernel line is drbd_main.c:4981. So the generation bump slips past the quorum=all SUSPEND, but it is NOT outside the divergence contract: a current-UUID bump IS the creation of a new data generation, and the kernel deliberately couples intended bumps to suspend state via the susp_uuid flag — so the unguarded :3807/:4471 sites firing on a still-frozen quorum-lost Primary are the LEAK PATH, contrary to (not exempt from) the contract.
final.does_minority_write_user_data: No. The minority writes ZERO user/application bytes. Proof (both verified against /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd): the ENTRY gate — may_inc_ap_bio() returns false under drbd_suspended() (drbd_int.h:2901-2906), so inc_ap_bio sleeps in wait_event and no request is even built (request alloc happens only AFTER inc_ap_bio returns, drbd_req.c:2301-2302); AND the SUBMIT gate — drbd_req.c:2057-2066 marks the request RQ_POSTPONED, bio_put's and NULLs private_bio, and `goto out`, so drbd_submit_req_private_bio() to ldev->backing_bdev is never called. Every local write funnels through these two chokepoints; there is no third path. The ONLY thing that hits disk on the minority is the metadata superblock holding the new current_uuid, on a physically separate block device (md_bdev). So Tommy's framing 'goes on writing' is FALSE for user data and TRUE only for one internal metadata bump.
final.voter_count_note: CAVEATED. For QOU_ALL the threshold equals the full voter count: quorum_at = voters (drbd_state.c:1370), and voters = qd.outdated + qd.quorumless + qd.unknown + qd.up_to_date + qd.present (VERIFIED drbd_state.c:1540, re-computed identically at :1551-1554). qd.diskless is NOT in that sum — a connected INTENTIONAL-diskless arbiter does NOT inflate the quorum=all denominator; it acts only as an even-split tiebreaker (drbd_state.c:1571-1576: even voter count + failed-by-exactly-one + majority of diskless connected). NOTE: a node that went diskless via disk FAILURE (want_bitmap=true) is still counted as 'present' (a voter); the diskless exclusion is for configured/intentional diskless only. So 'needs all 4' is correct-by-design IF AND ONLY IF the 4th member is DISKFUL. OPEN ITEM Tommy must resolve: is Bedrock's arbiter resource's 4th member diskful, or intentional-diskless+tiebreaker? If diskless, LINBIT explicitly recommends an absolute numeric quorum rather than majority/all (DRBD's diskful-node count is heuristic). TWO further caveats from verification: (a) default is QOU_OFF — a config typo leaves quorum OFF entirely, in which case have_quorum is forced true (drbd_state.c:2436-2439) and NOTHING is enforced; (b) the even-split diskless tiebreaker at :1571-1576 can flip a 2-of-X even partition back to quorate, so 'quorum-less' is not unconditional on even voter counts. To VERIFY quorum=all is actually in effect: `drbdsetup show <res> --show-defaults` must show `quorum all;` + `on-no-quorum suspend-io;`, and `drbdsetup status --verbose` should show resource 'suspended:quorum' + per-device quorum:no on the minority. The fact that you OBSERVED 'suspended:quorum' already proves it is in effect on this resource — make that the standing check.
final.plain_answer: Yes — quorum=all is doing real work, it is not nothing. Its job is to stop a minority from writing user data that would diverge, and on your 2-of-4 minority it does that completely: every application write is frozen (entry-blocked in inc_ap_bio, and any in-flight write is postponed with its disk-bound bio thrown away before it can reach the backing disk), so ZERO user bytes hit disk. The 'new current UUID: CB50...' you saw is NOT a user-data write — it is a metadata-only generation bump written to the separate metadata superblock on a worker/state-change code path that the suspend (quorum=all + suspend-io) never gates. So the minority does NOT 'go on writing' anything the cluster's data set cares about; it writes one UUID into its own metadata. Why scenario A (lose ALL peers) didn't bump but B (keep one peer) did: the bump needs a surviving peer slot to rotate the old UUID into, and the worker dispatch path is itself have_quorum-gated — so only the state-change path (with a remaining peer, sites :3807/:4471, which are NOT quorum-gated) fires. Bottom line on safety: quorum=all = no divergent COMMITTED DATA, and that guarantee holds. But correct the earlier framing — this UUID bump is NOT 'documented intended / harmless'; a current-UUID rotation IS a new data generation, and the kernel deliberately couples legitimate bumps to the suspend (susp_uuid) state. A frozen, quorum-lost Primary bumping its UUID is the UNGUARDED leak path, contrary to the divergence-avoidance contract. It is data-SAFE (no bytes diverge), but it is a real defect: on reconnect it can force an unnecessary full resync or look like split-brain (your already-logged lesson_drbd_uuid_rotation_quorum). The durable fix is a kernel-side have_quorum guard at drbd_state.c:3807/:4471, not a data-safety emergency.
load_bearing_claims: DATA freeze VERIFIED verbatim at /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd/drbd_req.c:2057-2066: `if (drbd_suspended(device)) { req->local_rq_state |= RQ_POSTPONED; if (req->private_bio) { bio_put(req->private_bio); req->private_bio = NULL; put_ldev(device); } goto out; }` — private_bio dropped before any submit, so drbd_submit_req_private_bio() to backing_bdev is never reached.

ENTRY gate VERIFIED: may_inc_ap_bio() returns false under drbd_suspended() (drbd_int.h:2901-2906); inc_ap_bio sleeps in wait_event and the request struct is allocated only AFTER inc_ap_bio returns (drbd_req.c:2301-2302) — a second, independent data-freeze that prevents even building a bio.

QOU_ALL threshold VERIFIED at /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd/drbd_state.c:1369-1370 `case QOU_ALL: quorum_at = voters;` — literally correct. CAVEAT: default is QOU_OFF (quorum disabled => have_quorum forced true, drbd_state.c:2436-2439); recommended setting is 'majority' which hits the voters/2+1 branch; and the even-split diskless tiebreaker (drbd_state.c:1571-1576) can make a 2-of-even partition quorate. So 2-of-4 is quorum-less under quorum=all with a diskful 4th member, but not unconditionally.

METADATA UUID leaf VERIFIED /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd/drbd_main.c:4947-4977 (__new_current_uuid_prepare): get_random_u64() + __drbd_uuid_set_current() + drbd_md_sync(); body has NO drbd_suspended/have_quorum/may_inc_ap_bio check. Log line drbd_main.c:4981 is `new current UUID: %016llX weak: %016llX` (synthesis truncated the ' weak:' suffix; cosmetic).

Metadata write goes to the SEPARATE md device (drbd_md_sync -> __drbd_md_sync -> drbd_md_write -> drbd_md_sync_page_io -> _drbd_md_sync_page_io, REQ_OP_WRITE on bdev->md_bdev via a raw submit_bio, drbd_actlog.c) — never enters drbd_submit_bio/__drbd_make_request/inc_ap_bio, so it is structurally outside the suspend gate. md_bdev is a separately-opened device distinct from backing_bdev (drbd_nl.c).

A/B asymmetry VERIFIED: state-change exec sites drbd_state.c:3807 and :4471 call drbd_uuid_new_current(device,false) with NO have_quorum guard, whereas the worker dispatch drbd_sender.c:3443 IS gated `if (device->have_quorum[NOW] && drbd_data_accessible(device, NOW))`. The bump DECISION (create_new_uuid) keys on role==R_PRIMARY && drbd_data_accessible() (local disk UpToDate), NOT have_quorum — VERIFIED drbd_state.c:3096-3136. drbd_data_accessible() (drbd_state.c:6379-6401) contains no have_quorum reference.

Voter denominator excludes intentional-diskless, VERIFIED drbd_state.c:1540 (and re-computed :1551-1554): no qd.diskless term; diskless is consulted ONLY in the even-split tiebreaker (:1571-1576). A node that became diskless via disk FAILURE is still counted as 'present' (a voter).

CORRECTED (was a REFUTED claim in synthesis): the disconnecting-Primary UUID bump is NOT a 'documented intended trigger outside the quorum contract.' A current-UUID rotation IS a new data generation; the kernel couples legitimate bumps to suspend state via susp_uuid (drbd_int.h:1038; gated in drbd_req.c:2262 _AFTER_ may_inc_ap_bio, and via drbd_sender.c:3443 have_quorum). A frozen, quorum-lost Primary bumping at the unguarded :3807/:4471 sites is the leak path, contrary to the divergence-avoidance contract — data-safe but a genuine defect.

Role is unchanged and safe: an existing Primary is NOT auto-demoted on quorum loss (only the data path is suspended; drbd_state.c:4463 merely invokes the 'quorum-lost' helper), and promotion of a fresh partition without quorum is refused with SS_NO_QUORUM (drbd_state.c:1757-1776), except under explicit operator `drbdadm primary --force`.

verdicts.claim: DATA freeze at /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd/drbd_req.c:2057-2066: when drbd_suspended(device) is true, the request is marked RQ_POSTPONED, its private_bio is bio_put/NULLed (put_ldev), and control jumps to 'out' — so drbd_submit_req_private_bio (the submit to ldev->backing_bdev) is never reached. This is the quorum-loss freeze path.
verdicts.evidence:
EXACT-MATCH: drbd_req.c:2057-2066 reads verbatim as quoted — L2057 `if (drbd_suspended(device)) {`, L2059 `req->local_rq_state |= RQ_POSTPONED;`, L2060-2064 `if (req->private_bio) { bio_put(req->private_bio); req->private_bio = NULL; put_ldev(device); }`, L2065 `goto out;` (in drbd_send_and_submit).

BACKING SUBMIT TRULY BYPASSED: The only caller of drbd_submit_req_private_bio() is drbd_req.c:2198, guarded by `if (submit_private_bio)`. drbd_submit_req_private_bio() is what binds the bio to the backing device and submits it (drbd_req.c:1831 `bio_set_dev(bio, device->ldev->backing_bdev)`, :1848 `submit_bio_noacct(bio)`). `submit_private_bio` is initialized false (drbd_req.c:2047) and set true ONLY at drbd_req.c:2171, which is itself gated by `if (req->private_bio)` at :2162. The suspend branch NULLs private_bio and `goto out` (:2187) lands AFTER line 2171, so submit_private_bio stays false and the backing submit at :2198 is skipped. Confirmed only-caller via grep: drbd_submit_req_private_bio appears at def :1817 and single call site :2198.

THIS IS THE QUORUM FREEZE: drbd_suspended() returns resource->cached_susp (drbd_int.h:2896-2899). cached_susp = resource_is_suspended(resource, NEW) (drbd_state.c:850), which is `susp_user || susp_nod || susp_quorum || susp_uuid` (drbd_state.c:247-248). susp_quorum is declared "IO suspended because no quorum" (drbd_int.h:1037) and set at drbd_state.c:2473-2474: `resource->susp_quorum[NEW] = resource->res_opts.on_no_quorum == ONQ_SUSPEND_IO ? !resource_has_quorum : false;`. So on-no-quorum=suspend-io + lost quorum => susp_quorum=true => cached_susp=true => drbd_suspended()=true => the L2057 freeze fires.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS FAILED: (1) Slow/AL-transaction path: do_submit worker (drbd_req.c:2543) -> submit_fast_path/send_and_submit_pending -> drbd_conflict_submit_write (:2442, :2520) -> drbd_send_and_submit (:2240), re-entering the SAME L2057 suspend check; it never submits the backing bio independently. (2) Conflict path drbd_conflict_submit_write (:2207-2249) either calls drbd_send_and_submit (re-checks suspend) or drops private_bio for postponed reqs (:2242-2246). No path reaches the backing device while suspended. The L2057 check is the single chokepoint every local write funnels through before any private_bio submit.

DOCS CORROBORATE: drbd.conf-9.0(5) manpage: "If a primary node should execute a write request, but the cluster partition has lost quorum, it will freeze IO or reject the write request with an error (depending on the on-no-quorum setting)." and "By default DRBD freezes IO on a device, that lost quorum." LINBIT user guide / manpage on on-no-quorum=suspend-io (default): "any process writing on a node without quorum will block until the node regains quorum." Matches the code's RQ_POSTPONED+freeze (no error to the app) exactly.

Files: /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd/drbd_req.c, /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd/drbd_int.h, /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd/drbd_state.c. Docs: https://manpages.debian.org/testing/drbd-utils/drbd.conf-9.0.5.en.html

verdicts.claim: ENTRY gate may_inc_ap_bio returns false under drbd_suspended() (drbd_int.h:2901-2906), so new app bios sleep in inc_ap_bio and never build a request — a second independent data-freeze enforcement.
verdicts.evidence:
Every link of the claim verifies against DRBD 9.3.2 source (/tmp/drbdsrc/drbd, HEAD a46cbd9) and the official manpage. I tried hard to refute and found only nuances that REFINE rather than break the claim.

1. The cited lines are exact. drbd_int.h:2901-2906:
  2901 static inline bool may_inc_ap_bio(struct drbd_device *device) {
  2903   if (device->cached_err_io) return true;
  2905   if (drbd_suspended(device)) return false;
And drbd_int.h:2896-2898: `drbd_suspended` returns `device->resource->cached_susp`.

2. The sleep + never-build-request chain holds literally. drbd_req.c __drbd_make_request (entry for every app bio):
  2294 void __drbd_make_request(...) {
  2301   inc_ap_bio(device, bio_data_dir(bio));        // sleeps here while suspended
  2302   req = drbd_request_prepare(device, bio, ...); // request struct is built only AFTER
inc_ap_bio (drbd_req.c:2281-2292) is `wait_event(device->misc_wait, inc_ap_bio_cond(device, rw))`. inc_ap_bio_cond (2251-2260) calls may_inc_ap_bio (2257) and `if (!rv) return false` (2259-2260), so wait_event keeps sleeping. The request is allocated in drbd_request_prepare->drbd_req_new->mempool_alloc (drbd_req.c:1896, :22), reached only after inc_ap_bio returns — so under suspend no request is built. Wording "sleep in inc_ap_bio and never build a request" is exact.

3. cached_susp genuinely covers quorum loss (the data-freeze in question). drbd_state.c:850 `resource->cached_susp = resource_is_suspended(resource, NEW)`; resource_is_suspended (245-248) ORs susp_user || susp_nod || susp_quorum || susp_uuid (plus susp_fen). susp_quorum[NEW] is set on quorum loss at drbd_state.c:2473-2474: `= res_opts.on_no_quorum == ONQ_SUSPEND_IO ? !resource_has_quorum : false`. Official manpage (drbd.conf-9.0): "By default DRBD freezes IO on a device, that lost quorum"; "when on-no-quorum is set to suspend-io, any process writing on a node without quorum will block until the node regains quorum" — matches the wait_event block exactly.

REFINEMENTS (do not refute the claim, but bound it):
- This freeze applies to the on-no-quorum=suspend-io policy only. Under on-no-quorum=io-error, cached_err_io is set (drbd_state.c:896-897) and (a) may_inc_ap_bio returns true early via the cached_err_io short-circuit at drbd_int.h:2903-2904, and (b) drbd_submit_bio rejects the bio with BLK_STS_IOERR at drbd_req.c:2766-2769 before ever reaching inc_ap_bio. So in io-error mode the bio does not sleep — it errors. The claim describes the default/suspend-io freeze, which is correct.
- "Second independent enforcement" is well-supported. There is a genuinely separate, redundant suspend check in the request path AFTER the request is built: drbd_send_and_submit at drbd_req.c:2057 `if (drbd_suspended(device))` marks the already-built req RQ_POSTPONED and pushes it back. So drbd_suspended() gates I/O at two independent points (entry inc_ap_bio at 2291/2257, and post-build send_and_submit at 2057), both keyed on the same cached_susp. Relative to the metadata-write path (drbd_md_sync), the may_inc_ap_bio entry gate is indeed a distinct, independent data-freeze enforcement.
- No bypass: the kernel block entry drbd_submit_bio (drbd_req.c:2748) funnels normal bios to __drbd_make_request (line 2787); the retry path do_retry also re-enters __drbd_make_request (drbd_main.c:3447) which again calls inc_ap_bio. There is no path that builds a normal app request without passing the inc_ap_bio gate.

Sources: /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd/drbd_int.h:2896-2921; drbd_req.c:2057, 2251-2310, 2748-2787, 1887-1896; drbd_state.c:245-254, 845-851, 2468-2474, 895-899; drbd_main.c:3447. Manpage drbd.conf-9.0 (manpages.debian.org/unstable/drbd-utils/drbd.conf-9.0.5.en.html).

verdicts.claim: QOU_ALL threshold VERIFIED at /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd/drbd_state.c:1369-1370 ('case QOU_ALL: quorum_at = voters;'), and therefore a 2-of-4 partition is correctly quorum-less.
verdicts.evidence:
PARTLY CORRECT BUT MIS-ATTRIBUTED. The literal source citation is exact and verified, but the reasoning rests on a non-default/wrong code path and omits the tiebreaker.

1) Literal lines confirmed verbatim — drbd_state.c:1361-1377:
  `static int calc_quorum_at(s32 setting, int voters){ ... case QOU_MAJORITY: quorum_at = voters / 2 + 1; break; case QOU_ALL: quorum_at = voters; break; default: quorum_at = setting; }`
So 1369-1370 is `case QOU_ALL: quorum_at = voters;` exactly as claimed.

2) But QOU_ALL is NOT the default and likely not the operative branch. drbd-headers/linux/drbd.h:444-446 define `QOU_OFF 0 / QOU_MAJORITY 1024 / QOU_ALL 1025`. drbd_limits.h:307: `#define DRBD_QUORUM_DEF QOU_OFF`. drbd_genl.h:149 wires the `quorum` option default to DRBD_QUORUM_DEF (=OFF). Confirmed by docs (drbdsetup-9.0 / drbd.conf-9.0 manpages): the quorum option "value might be set to off, majority, all or a numeric value" and "defaults to off." The standard recommendation is `majority`, which hits the OTHER branch (line 1366-1367, voters/2+1), not the cited QOU_ALL line.

3) When quorum is OFF (the default), calc_quorum_at / calc_quorum are never reached at all — drbd_state.c:2436-2439: `if (resource->res_opts.quorum != QOU_OFF) device->have_quorum[NEW] = calc_quorum(...); else device->have_quorum[NEW] = true;`. So the cited line only runs if an operator explicitly set `quorum all`.

4) The OUTCOME ("2-of-4 quorum-less") does hold under both enabled settings: in calc_quorum (drbd_state.c:1556,1568-1569) with voters=4, quorum_at = 3 for majority or 4 for all; the test `(qd.up_to_date + qd.present) >= quorum_at` fails for a 2-node partition either way. So 2-of-4 is quorum-less — but the claim 'verifies' it via a line that is dead code under the default and under the recommended `majority` setting.

5) Refuting nuance the claim omits: the even-split TIEBREAKER at drbd_state.c:1571-1576 can make a 2-of-4 partition quorate: `if (!have_quorum && voters!=0 && voters%2==0 && qd.up_to_date+qd.present == quorum_at-1 && qd.diskless >= diskless_majority_at && device->have_quorum[NOW]) { have_quorum = true; ... "Would lose quorum, but using tiebreaker logic to keep" }`. So '2-of-4 is *correctly* quorum-less' is not unconditional — a diskless tiebreaker holding the previously-quorate partition flips it to quorate.

CONCLUSION: The file:line citation is literally accurate (verdict not REFUTED), but the claim is mis-scoped: QOU_ALL is the non-default branch (default is QOU_OFF; recommended is majority→voters/2+1), and 'correctly quorum-less' ignores the diskless-tiebreaker exception. Treat the cited line as correct trivia, not as the mechanism that makes 2-of-4 quorum-less in a default/majority config.

verdicts.evidence:
Verified against DRBD 9.3.2 source at HEAD a46cbd9 (/tmp/drbdsrc/drbd, identical to /home/tommy/projects/drbdsrc_clone). Tried hard to refute by checking for any inc_ap_bio / __drbd_make_request / suspend entry in the MD path and for re-entry of the DRBD device via the raw submit_bio — none exists.

CALL CHAIN EXACTLY AS CLAIMED:
- drbd_md_sync() -> __drbd_md_sync(device, false) (drbd_main.c:4678-4681, 4645).
- __drbd_md_sync -> drbd_md_write(device, buffer) (drbd_main.c:4666).
- drbd_md_write -> "err = drbd_md_sync_page_io(device, device->ldev, sector, REQ_OP_WRITE);" (drbd_main.c:4631).
- drbd_md_sync_page_io -> _drbd_md_sync_page_io(device, bdev, sector, op) (drbd_actlog.c:159).
- _drbd_md_sync_page_io: "bio = bio_alloc_bioset(bdev->md_bdev, 1, op | op_flags, GFP_NOIO, &drbd_md_io_bio_set);" (drbd_actlog.c:101) then raw "submit_bio(bio);" (drbd_actlog.c:127). op is REQ_OP_WRITE. So the write bio is built on bdev->md_bdev and submitted directly.

SEPARATE MD DEVICE: md_bdev is a distinct, separately-opened lower-level block device. drbd_nl.c opens meta_dev independently of backing_dev: "file = open_backing_dev(device, new_disk_conf->meta_dev, meta_claim_ptr);" -> "nbc->md_bdev = file_bdev(file);" (drbd_nl.c:2951,2966), while backing_dev is opened at drbd_nl.c:2925. Code explicitly distinguishes them: "ldev->md_bdev != ldev->backing_bdev" (drbd_nl.c:2885) and the external-MD check at drbd_nl.c:3387. struct fields are separate: "struct block_device *md_bdev;" (drbd_int.h:773). Official docs confirm: meta-disk "can be internal, meaning that the lower-level device contains both the data and the metadata, or on a separate device" (drbd.conf-9.0 meta-disk option). Since the raw submit_bio targets md_bdev (the lower-level meta device, not the DRBD gendisk whose private_data is the drbd_device), it does NOT re-enter drbd_submit_bio.

BYPASSES __drbd_make_request / inc_ap_bio: grep of drbd_actlog.c (which holds _drbd_md_sync_page_io) shows inc_ap_bio appears 0 times; __drbd_make_request and inc_ap_bio are confined to drbd_req.c. These are exclusively on the application-data path: the DRBD virtual device registers ".submit_bio = drbd_submit_bio" (drbd_main.c:182) -> drbd_submit_bio -> "__drbd_make_request(device, bio, ...)" (drbd_req.c:2787) -> "inc_ap_bio(device, bio_data_dir(bio));" (drbd_req.c:2301). That user path submits the local bio to the BACKING device: "req->private_bio = bio_alloc_clone(device->ldev->backing_bdev, bio, ...)" (drbd_req.c:1906), "bio_set_dev(bio, device->ldev->backing_bdev)" (drbd_req.c:1831), then submit_bio_noacct (drbd_req.c:1848). The MD path never calls drbd_submit_bio, __drbd_make_request, or inc_ap_bio.

STRUCTURALLY DISTINCT FROM SUSPEND GATING (the load-bearing consequence): the quorum/suspend gate lives only in the inc_ap_bio path. inc_ap_bio -> inc_ap_bio_cond -> may_inc_ap_bio (drbd_int.h:2900), which does "if (drbd_suspended(device)) return false;" and "if (atomic_read(&device->suspend_cnt)) return false;" (drbd_int.h:2905-2908). drbd_suspended() returns resource->cached_susp (drbd_int.h:2895). on-no-quorum=suspend-io "freezes IO on a device that lost quorum" (drbd.conf-9.0 on-no-quorum option) via this cached_susp flag. Because the MD write never enters inc_ap_bio, it is not gated by drbd_suspended()/susp_quorum — confirming the path is structurally distinct from the suspendable backing_bdev user-data path.

Both source clones are byte-identical (sizes match) and at the stated HEAD a46cbd9. Official docs corroborate separate meta-disk and suspend-io quorum semantics (LINBIT drbd.conf-9.0 manpage; DRBD 9 User Guide 2.23 DRBD quorum / section 16 DRBD metadata).

verdicts.claim: A/B asymmetry VERIFIED: state-change exec sites drbd_state.c:3807 and :4471 call drbd_uuid_new_current(device,false) UNGUARDED, whereas the worker path drbd_sender.c:3443-3444 IS gated 'if (device->have_quorum[NOW] && drbd_data_accessible(device, NOW)) drbd_uuid_new_current(...)'. The bump decision is set on drbd_data_accessible() (local disk UpToDate), not have_quorum (drbd_state.c:3094-3135).
verdicts.evidence:
Verified against the locally-cloned DRBD source at /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd (REL_VERSION "9.3.2", git HEAD a46cbd9, dated 2026-06-01; /home/tommy/projects/drbdsrc_clone matches identically). Every line number in the claim is exact, and the quoted code is verbatim. I tried hard to refute the asymmetry and could not; the docs corroborate the design intent that makes it a real gap.

CALL SITE A (worker path, GATED) — /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd/drbd_sender.c:3437-3445, function drbd_check_peers_new_current_uuid():
  3443  if (device->have_quorum[NOW] && drbd_data_accessible(device, NOW))

This is reached via make_new_current_uuid() (sender.c:3447-3452) -> do_device_work() on the MAKE_NEW_CUR_UUID work bit (sender.c:3461-3462). The have_quorum[NOW] conjunct is present verbatim as the claim states.

CALL SITE B1 (state.c:3807, UNGUARDED) — /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd/drbd_state.c, function check_may_resume_io_after_fencing():
  3804  if (test_and_clear_bit(NEW_CUR_UUID, &device->flags)) {
  3805    kref_get(&device->kref);
  3806    rcu_read_unlock();
  3807    drbd_uuid_new_current(device, false);
Gated only on the NEW_CUR_UUID flag and all_peer_disks_outdated (the outdate-peer-handler-succeeded branch, line 3800), with NO have_quorum check at or before the call.

CALL SITE B2 (state.c:4471, UNGUARDED) — /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd/drbd_state.c, function w_after_state_change():
  4466  if (!susp_uuid[OLD] && susp_uuid[NEW] &&

  4470  if (new_current_uuid)

new_current_uuid is driven solely by the susp_uuid edge + NEW_CUR_UUID flag; there is NO have_quorum[NOW] guard. (Note: the same function has two further unguarded sites the claim did not list — :4301 and :4305 — set on peer-disk-goes-Failed/Inconsistent and local-disk-Failed-while-Primary; these only reinforce, not weaken, the asymmetry.)

DECISION LOGIC keyed on drbd_data_accessible(), NOT have_quorum — /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd/drbd_state.c sanitize/decision block (claim's cited 3094-3135), exact text:
  3096  if (lost_contact_to_peer_data(peer_disk_state)) {
  3097    if (role[NEW] == R_PRIMARY && !test_bit(UNREGISTERED, &device->flags) &&
  3098        drbd_data_accessible(device, NEW))
  3099      create_new_uuid = true;
  ...
  3128  if (... role[NEW] == R_PRIMARY && drbd_data_accessible(device, NEW))
  3129    create_new_uuid = true;
  3131  if (role[OLD] == R_SECONDARY && role[NEW] == R_PRIMARY)
  3132    create_new_uuid = true;
  3135  if (create_new_uuid && !susp_uuid[OLD])
  3136    set_bit(__NEW_CUR_UUID, &device->flags);
Every create_new_uuid predicate keys on role[NEW]==R_PRIMARY and drbd_data_accessible(), never have_quorum[NEW].

DECISIVE — drbd_data_accessible() does NOT consult quorum (drbd_state.c:6379-6401):
  6384  if (device->disk_state[which] == D_UP_TO_DATE)
  6385    return true;   // local disk UpToDate alone => accessible
  ...for_each_peer_device: returns true if any peer disk is D_UP_TO_DATE.
There is no have_quorum[] reference in this function. So a quorum-lost Primary whose local disk is still UpToDate evaluates drbd_data_accessible()==true and arms the bump.

TRIGGER ties bump to quorum/contact loss — lost_contact_to_peer_data() (drbd_state.c:3744-3751):
  3749  return (os >= D_INCONSISTENT && os != D_UNKNOWN && os != D_OUTDATED)
  3750    && (ns < D_INCONSISTENT || ns == D_UNKNOWN || ns == D_OUTDATED);
i.e. true exactly when a peer's data goes from reachable to lost (the partition/quorum-loss event), which then arms create_new_uuid for a still-data-accessible Primary at line 3097-3099 with no quorum guard.

DEFER/CARRY mechanism is consistent with the claim, not a refutation: when the state change itself makes the resource suspended, the __NEW_CUR_UUID set bit is carried to NEW_CUR_UUID (drbd_state.c:902-908) and converted into susp_uuid[NEW] (drbd_state.c:2476-2484), then later actually emitted at the unguarded site :4466-4471 when susp_uuid rises. The emission site still lacks the have_quorum[NOW] conjunct present on the worker path.

ATTEMPT TO REFUTE (failed): I checked whether something upstream blocks reaching :3807/:4471 without quorum. It does not — the decision predicates (3097-3132) only require role[NEW]==R_PRIMARY + drbd_data_accessible(), and the after-fencing branch (3800) requires only all_peer_disks_outdated. None gate on have_quorum, unlike sender.c:3443. Git history is squashed into the merge commit a46cbd9 so per-line blame dates are unavailable, but the source text is unambiguous.

DOCS corroborate this is a meaningful asymmetry (drbdsetup-9.0 manpage, https://manpages.debian.org/testing/drbd-utils/drbdsetup-9.0.8.en.html, and DRBD 9 user guide https://linbit.com/drbd-user-guide/drbd-guide-9_0-en/): on-no-quorum default 'By default DRBD freezes IO on a device, that lost quorum'; new-current-uuid 'Generate a new current UUID and rotates all other UUID values', the current UUID being the data-generation identifier; and the documented model is that a 'primary node loses quorum hence has all IO requests frozen ... connects to another, quorate partition ... started a newer data-generation there' — i.e., a NEW data generation is supposed to originate in the QUORATE partition. A quorum-lost Primary rotating its current-UUID via the unguarded state-change sites is therefore exactly the documented-as-undesirable behavior, matching the operator's memory note lesson_drbd_uuid_rotation_quorum.md. The worker path's have_quorum[NOW] conjunct enforces the documented intent; the state-change exec sites at :3807/:4471 do not.

CONCLUSION: All four sub-claims hold with exact line numbers and verbatim code: (A) worker path is quorum-gated, (B) :3807 and :4471 are not, (C) call argument is (device,false) at all three, and (D) the bump decision keys on drbd_data_accessible()/local-UpToDate rather than have_quorum. Verdict CONFIRMED.

verdicts.claim: Voter denominator excludes diskless, VERIFIED drbd_state.c:1540: 'voters = qd.outdated + qd.quorumless + qd.unknown + qd.up_to_date + qd.present' (no qd.diskless term); diskless arbiter is tiebreaker-only.
verdicts.evidence:
VERSION: /tmp/drbdsrc HEAD a46cbd9440cb9968b369b11e60338180b8a3912d (DRBD 9, matches the cited a46cbd9).

(1) LINE-EXACT MATCH. /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd/drbd_state.c:1540 reads verbatim (cat -A confirmed, leading tab):
  "voters = qd.outdated + qd.quorumless + qd.unknown + qd.up_to_date + qd.present;"
No qd.diskless term, exactly as claimed.

(2) NOT A ONE-LINE FLUKE — diskless is excluded at BOTH voter-computation points. The same function calc_quorum() (drbd_state.c:1525-1586) recomputes voters a second time at lines 1551-1554:
  1551  if (qd.unknown)
  1552      voters = qd.outdated + qd.quorumless + qd.unknown + qd.up_to_date + qd.present;
  1553  else
  1554      voters = qd.up_to_date + qd.present;
Neither branch includes qd.diskless or qd.missing_diskless.

(3) qd.diskless IS A DISTINCT STRUCT FIELD, never summed into voters. struct quorum_detail (drbd_state.c:31-40) has separate ints {up_to_date, present, outdated, diskless, missing_diskless, quorumless, unknown, quorate_peers}. Grep of all qd.diskless/qd->diskless uses in the file shows it is referenced ONLY at:
  - line 1557: diskless_majority_at = calc_quorum_at(QOU_MAJORITY, qd.diskless + qd.missing_diskless)  -- a SEPARATE threshold, not the voter set
  - line 1575: the tiebreaker condition.

(4) "TIEBREAKER-ONLY" CONFIRMED by the gating logic at lines 1571-1576:
  1571  if (!have_quorum && voters != 0 && voters % 2 == 0 && qd.up_to_date + qd.present == quorum_at - 1 &&
  1575      qd.diskless >= diskless_majority_at && device->have_quorum[NOW]) {
  1576      have_quorum = true;
Diskless votes are consulted ONLY when: quorum was otherwise lost, the (diskful) voter count is EVEN, and the partition failed by exactly one vote. Comment lines 1572-1574: "It is an even number of nodes (think 2) and we failed by one vote. ... Using the diskless nodes a tie-breaker!" The primary have_quorum decision (lines 1568-1569) is computed purely from up_to_date/present vs quorum_at/min_redundancy_at — disk-bearing nodes only.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS (all failed to break the claim, one nuance worth noting):
- Tried: does an UNINTENTIONALLY diskless node (real disk failure, want_bitmap=true) sneak into the denominator? In __calc_quorum_with_disk (line 1448) only "disk_state==D_DISKLESS && is_intentional_diskless" goes to qd->diskless; a connected unintentional-diskless peer falls to the else -> qd->present++ (counts as voter). So "voters excludes diskless" is precisely true for INTENTIONAL diskless (the arbiter/tiebreaker case the claim is about); a node whose disk failed is still treated as a present voter. This does not contradict the claim, which speaks of the diskless arbiter.
- is_intentional_diskless = !want_bitmap(peer_device) (drbd_state.c:1418,1487; want_bitmap def in drbd_main.c returns pdc->bitmap). Confirms the diskless/voter split keys off configured (intentional) disklessness.

OFFICIAL DOCS — all corroborate:
- LINBIT blog "DRBD Quorum Implementation Updates": "In a cluster with an even number of nodes with backing storage (think: two), a partition that has precisely half of the nodes may keep quorum when it also has contact with the majority of the diskless nodes (think: one)." and "An important detail is a partition of half of the nodes with storage can never gain quorum when it establishes connections to diskless nodes." This is exactly the even-count, failed-by-one tiebreaker behavior at code lines 1571-1575.
- drbdsetup-9.0(8) manpage (manpages.debian.org): "Every node with a disk directly connected to the node that should be promoted counts." i.e. the voter set is disk-bearing nodes; and it warns that for permanently diskless nodes to gain quorum you should specify an absolute number rather than majority/all because DRBD's count of diskful nodes is heuristic.
- DRBD 9.0 User Guide quorum chapter: a third node acting as arbitrator "can be diskless" and "act as a quorum tiebreaker."

CONCLUSION: Both factual sub-claims hold — (a) the voter denominator at drbd_state.c:1540 (and its re-computation at 1552/1554) excludes the diskless count, and (b) the diskless arbiter participates only through the separate even-split, off-by-one tiebreaker branch (1571-1575), never as a normal voter. Sole caveat: this applies to intentional/configured diskless nodes; a node that became diskless via disk failure is still counted as 'present' (a voter), which is consistent with the claim's framing about the diskless arbiter.

verdicts.claim: LINBIT's quorum contract is DATA-scoped only ("the replicated data set is not touched, so that the node does not create a diverging data set"; suspend-io "suspends all queued and future I/O operations"); the docs make no claim about UUID/metadata, so a disconnecting-Primary UUID bump is OUTSIDE (not a violation of) the quorum contract, and is a documented intended trigger for a new data generation.
verdicts.evidence:
VERBATIM-QUOTE ACCURACY (partly supports the claim's premise): Both quoted phrases are real and verbatim from the LINBIT blog "Using the DRBD Quorum Feature as an Alternative to Fencing in a Pacemaker Cluster" (https://linbit.com/blog/using-the-drbd-quorum-feature-as-an-alternative-to-fencing-in-a-pacemaker-cluster/): "The suspend-io action suspends all queued and future I/O operations to the backing DRBD device." and "However, a node that does not have quorum needs to guarantee that the replicated data set is not touched, so that the node does not create a diverging data set." The DRBD 9.0 User Guide phrases quorum's purpose the same way: "...the DRBD quorum feature helps you avoid a situation that would create a diverging data set." The drbdsetup-9.0(8) man page (https://manpages.debian.org/testing/drbd-utils/drbdsetup-9.0.8.en.html) on-no-quorum/suspend-io text and the on-suspended-primary-outdated text do NOT contain a sentence directly equating quorum protection with "UUID/metadata." So the claim's narrow observation (the docs' literal wording is data/IO-phrased) is TRUE.

WHY THE CONCLUSION IS REFUTED:
(1) A current-UUID bump IS the creation of a new data generation, not metadata orthogonal to "the data set." drbd_main.c:5273 drbd_uuid_new_current() writes the exposed/current UUID and sends it to peers; DRBD's own term for a fresh current UUID is a new "data generation" (echoed in the man page: a quorate peer "started a newer data-generation there"). The contract's stated goal — "does not create a diverging data set" — is tracked precisely by these generation UUIDs, so a UUID bump is INSIDE the divergence contract, not outside it. Calling it "outside" is a category error.

(2) The kernel deliberately COUPLES UUID bumps to the IO-suspend (quorum) state via a dedicated flag, contradicting "docs/contract make no claim about UUID/metadata": drbd_int.h:1038 "bool susp_uuid[2];  /* IO suspended because waiting new current UUID */"; resource_is_suspended() = susp_user || susp_quorum || susp_uuid (drbd_state.c:248). The intended bump is GATED on suspend state: drbd_state.c:3134-3136 "/* Only a single new current uuid when susp_uuid becomes true */ if (create_new_uuid && !susp_uuid[OLD]) set_bit(__NEW_CUR_UUID...)", and drbd_req.c:2262-2265 "check need for new current uuid _AFTER_ ensuring IO is not suspended via may_inc_ap_bio". may_inc_ap_bio() returns false when drbd_suspended() (drbd_int.h:2901-2906). So the intended trigger fires on the susp_uuid OLD->NEW resume/regain-data-access edge (drbd_state.c:4466-4471 new_current_uuid -> drbd_uuid_new_current), and the man page's documented scenario is the quorum-lost primary CONNECTING TO A QUORATE PARTITION and learning it is outdated (--on-suspended-primary-outdated). The documented intended new-generation trigger is the connected/quorate transition — NOT a free bump by a still-frozen, quorum-lost Primary.

(3) The bump by a still-quorum-lost Primary is the UNGUARDED leak path, not the documented trigger: drbd_state.c:4466 (per the user's own RCA lesson lesson_drbd_uuid_rotation_quorum) — a frozen quorum-lost Primary that still retains a peer rotates current-UUID via the internal state-change 2PC, which bypasses the susp_uuid/may_inc_ap_bio gate that protects the normal path. Labeling this as "documented intended" inverts intended (gated, resume-time) vs. leaked (frozen, unguarded). Conclusion: the UUID bump by a quorum-lost Primary is inside, and contrary to, the divergence-avoidance contract; it is not an out-of-scope, intended new-generation trigger. (Source HEAD: /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd, 9.3.2, a46cbd9.)

verdicts.claim: Role is unchanged: an existing Primary is NOT auto-demoted on quorum loss (only the data path is suspended); promotion of a fresh partition without quorum is refused (SS_NO_QUORUM).
verdicts.evidence:
Verified against DRBD 9.3.2 source (HEAD a46cbd9) at /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd and corroborated by LINBIT docs. I tried hard to refute and could not; the only role-demotion paths are unrelated (split-brain handlers and an opt-in, non-default setting).

PART A — Primary is NOT auto-demoted on quorum loss; only the data path is suspended.
- /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd/drbd_state.c:4463-4464 is the exact quorum-loss-while-Primary handler: `if (role[NEW] == R_PRIMARY && have_quorum[OLD] && !have_quorum[NEW]) drbd_maybe_khelper(device, NULL, "quorum-lost");`. The condition asserts the node is STILL Primary (role[NEW]==R_PRIMARY) after losing quorum; the only action is invoking a userspace helper. No role change to Secondary exists in this path.
- The data path (not the role) is what gets suspended: drbd_state.c:2473-2474 `resource->susp_quorum[NEW] = resource->res_opts.on_no_quorum == ONQ_SUSPEND_IO ? !resource_has_quorum : false;`. This susp_quorum flag feeds resource_is_suspended() (drbd_state.c:245-248, OR of susp_user|susp_nod|susp_quorum|susp_uuid) -> cached_susp -> drbd_suspended() (drbd_int.h:2896-2899). In the request path, drbd_req.c:2057 `if (drbd_suspended(device)) { req->local_rq_state |= RQ_POSTPONED; ... }` — writes are held/retried, i.e. IO frozen, role untouched. Default on-no-quorum is suspend-io (drbd_limits.h:321 `#define DRBD_ON_NO_QUORUM_DEF ONQ_SUSPEND_IO`).
- Comment at drbd_receiver.c:5176-5177 reinforces the model: resync direction is decided by "looking if a node lost quorum WHILE BEING PRIMARY" — DRBD explicitly tracks a node that stayed Primary through quorum loss.
- Refutation attempts ruled out: the two change_role(R_SECONDARY) calls (drbd_receiver.c:4405 "after-sb-1pri", 4459 "after-sb-2pri") are split-brain after-sb-Npri ASB_CALL_HELPER recovery, not quorum loss. drbd_receiver.c:864 force_demote is connect-time data-divergence handling. drbd_receiver.c:8089-8099 maybe_force_secondary is gated on on_susp_primary_outdated==SPO_FORCE_SECONDARY (a non-default, opt-in setting; default is 'disconnect') and only fires after a DIFFERENT partition was promoted (which itself needed quorum). Docs confirm: drbd.conf-9.0(5) manpage states "By default DRBD freezes IO on a device, that lost quorum" (not demotes); LINBIT docs confirm on-suspended-primary-outdated defaults to 'disconnect' and only force-secondary demotes, and only when the primary learns another partition started a newer data generation.

PART B — Promotion of a fresh partition without quorum is refused with SS_NO_QUORUM.
- /tmp/drbdsrc/drbd/drbd_state.c:1757-1776: `/* Prevent promote when there is no quorum ... */ if ((role[OLD] == R_SECONDARY || device->have_quorum[OLD]) && role[NEW] == R_PRIMARY && !device->have_quorum[NEW]) { ... return SS_NO_QUORUM; }`. SS_NO_QUORUM is defined at drbd-headers/linux/drbd.h:337 (= -25), string "No quorum" at drbd-headers/drbd_strings.c:104.
- This check lives in __is_valid_soft_transition (block from drbd_state.c:1627), reached via is_valid_soft_transition (1870) from end_state_change (631-633). Every promotion routes through it: manual drbdadm primary -> change_role (drbd_nl.c:1115) and auto-promote (drbd_main.c open path). Docs confirm: drbd.conf-9.0(5) quorum option states "a node in the cluster partition can only be promoted to primary if the cluster partition has quorum."
- Closest refutation: drbd_nl.c:1198 `if (rv == SS_NO_QUORUM && force && !(flags & CS_FP_OUTDATE_PEERS))` lets `drbdadm primary --force` override SS_NO_QUORUM by outdating peers. This is an explicit operator --force action, not automatic promotion of a fresh partition, so it does not contradict the claim's scope (normal/unforced promotion is refused).
